subject: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal

Team — quick escalation after the call with ClearPath this morning. They’re requesting three commercial items that touch on our high-risk guardrails:

- 30% up-front enterprise discount on list for a 3-year commitment (opportunity ~ $1.2M ARR over term)
- Request for a territorial exclusivity in US-West for the logistics vertical (they say it’s to secure channel partner commitments) for 12 months
- An MFN-style clause: they want assurance we won’t offer a lower price to certain named competitors for the same scope for 6 months following signature (they called it a “price floor / parity guarantee”)

Attached: ClearPath_MOA_draft_v3.pdf and our pricing-sheet.xlsx.

Asking for explicit guidance so I can return a firm counter today:
1) Discount ceiling we can approve here (with AD signoff vs exec)
2) Whether we can accept any exclusivity language and if so what scope/duration
3) Whether we can accept the MFN-lite ask and if so what wording/legal controls to require

Risks/notes: exclusivity + MFN together creates market lock concerns and sets a precedent. MFN as written in their doc is broad and would force us to disclose competitor win prices (not acceptable). I’ve proposed a narrower approach below but need legal and revenue guidance.

Proposed quick counter (if allowed): 25% discount with $900k ARR commit; priority-onboarding window of 6 months (not a geography-wide exclusivity); MFN-lite limited to published list prices and equivalent contract configurations (no retroactive catch-all).

If we can’t land on this, I recommend we push pricing/priority in exchange for a short pilot exclusivity, and explicitly reject any broad MFN.

Thanks — I’m on standby to jump on a call.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal

Jordan — thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I weigh in:

1) Is the 30% ask on top of the discount tiers in pricing-sheet.xlsx or replacing them? Please confirm effective list and final net ARR you expect.
2) Are they requesting exclusivity for Redwood across all products or only the inference/runtime product for the logistics workflows (we should be explicit).
3) Do they want any breach/penalty language tied to exclusivity?
4) Any customer references they cite that require MFN (eg: are they asking because a partner promised them parity elsewhere)?

If the 30% is additive and the exclusivity is wide, I’m inclined to push back hard. If the exclusivity is narrowly scoped to a pilot/priority onboarding for specific accounts we can probably accept a shorter window.

I’ll hold a pending signoff but want legal’s take on MFN wording first.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal

Quick answers:
- 30% replaces the standard list-tier for this deal as they’re asking for a bespoke enterprise package (net expected year-1 ARR ~$300k, total committed over contract $1.08M).
- Exclusivity ask is specifically for the logistics workflow on our inference product and they’ve framed it as limited to US-West accounts they bring to us over the next 12 months. They explicitly asked for no carve-outs.
- They asked us to include a 12-month break fee (unspecified) if we violate exclusivity.
- Their rationale for MFN: they’re in discussions with two channel partners who may resell in other regions; they fear we’ll offer lower prices to those partners and want parity for 6 months.

I attached a short proposed_exclusivity_clause.txt with narrowly limited language: 6-month priority onboarding window (not a geographic exclusivity), scoped to named pilot accounts, and terminates if customer doesn’t meet onboarding milestones.

I’m leaning to counter with Marissa’s guidance below if you agree.

-J

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal

Jordan / team — scanned their draft MOA and attached legal_redline_ClearPath_MOA.docx with redlines. Key legal points:

- Do NOT accept their MFN as written. It is open-ended and would require us to disclose confidential pricing.
- If we agree to any MFN-lite, it must be: (a) limited to public/published list price (no confidential customer-to-customer comparisons), (b) limited to the same contract term and seat/usage tiers, (c) include an explicit carve-out for pre-existing negotiated enterprise deals, and (d) capped at 6 months max.
- Exclusivity: legal will not sign off on broad territorial exclusivity. We can accept a limited "priority implementation" clause tied to named pilot accounts and explicit milestones; include termination for failure to meet milestones and a mutual no-solicit for partner contacts for the same time window.
- We should add audit rights tied to MFN (to confirm published list price), and a mutual confidentiality clause for any pricing disclosures.

I marked up specific language in the docx. If the business insists on broader MFN we should escalate to Execs and require additional underwriting (higher commit, stronger break fee, and escrowed penalties).

-rm
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: priority access + price-floor (MFN-lite) — clearance for counterproposal

Thanks team — quick commercial view:
- Approve up to 25% discount conditional on a minimum $900k ARR commit over 24 months and standard payment milestones.
- Do NOT approve a 12-month territorial exclusivity across US-West. We will compromise with a 6-month priority onboarding window limited to named pilot accounts and subject to milestone completion.
- MFN: acceptable only in the narrow MFN-lite form Rishi outlined (published list price, same term/config, 6-month cap, carve-outs for pre-existing deals).

If ClearPath accepts these controls we avoid Exec escalation. If they push for more (12-month full exclusivity or broad MFN) escalate to me and I’ll route to the CRO/CEO for an exception (requires stronger economics and legal indemnities).

Please prepare the counter and send to ClearPath with the redline and the DocuSign link.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anika Shah <anika@clearpath.ai>, David Chu <dchu@clearpath.ai>, procurement@clearpath.ai
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood counter: priority onboarding + MFN-lite + commercial commitment (ClearPath)

Anika / David — thanks again for the call. We had an internal review and can move forward with a limited counter-proposal: please see highlights below and redline attached.

- Pricing: we can extend a 25% enterprise discount (finalized in attached MOA) in exchange for a $900k ARR commitment over 24 months and standard payment milestones.
- Priority onboarding: we will provide a 6-month priority implementation window for named pilot accounts you bring to us (detailed in the MOA). This is NOT a broad territorial exclusivity; it is tied to the named accounts and milestone completion.
- MFN-lite: we will accept a limited price-parity commitment that is restricted to published list prices for equivalent product/term/configuration and capped at 6 months after signature. Pre-existing negotiated enterprise agreements are carved out. We will add audit rights to verify published pricing.

Attached: legal_redline_ClearPath_MOA.docx (our redlines) and the updated pricing-sheet.xlsx. If you’re comfortable with these points I’ll send the DocuSign link for signature: https://www.docusign.com/contract/clearpath-moa-v3

If you need broader exclusivity or a longer MFN term we’ll need to escalate for an exception and discuss additional commercial commitments.

Looking forward — can you confirm by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: legal_redline_ClearPath_MOA.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), pricing-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
